assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin therapies that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with additional cardiovascular and renal benefit. The chain from peptide discovery to a drug class with very large clinical impact is clear and exceptionally strong.
assessment.attribution: Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form), Holst (human physiology and secretion) and Drucker (biology, intestinotrophic and therapeutic actions) are the most defensible trio. Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues is also major and is left out only because of the three-person limit. Credit also involves others not on the list (for example Habener), so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed by many independent trials and by wide clinical use over nearly two decades; timing is clearly mature, and delay carries growing risk of mis-allocation.
uncertainties: Fair split between basic discovery and drug development, and between Mojsov and others, is unsettled.
Long-term safety and full cardiometabolic effects are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. The concept is original and the clinical impact is demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early CAR clinical work) are credible; the original CAR concept by Eshhar is not in the supplied names, which weakens the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year remissions provide independent confirmation, though toxicity, cost and limited solid-tumour efficacy remain.
uncertainties: Eshhar's priority is not among the credited names.
Benefit in solid tumours and long-term safety are not established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with light and is a transformative experimental tool across physiology. The originality and lasting methodological impact are high; direct patient benefit is so far limited.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation by Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg), and neuronal deployment by Boyden and Deisseroth, make a fair three-person configuration hard; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photoactivation adds complexity. I choose Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann as the strongest compromise.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over fifteen years; first clinical vision-restoration applications are emerging. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among six plausible contributors is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and rational BCR-ABL inhibition turned chronic myeloid leukemia from fatal to a chronic manageable disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Impact is major and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug discovery programme), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio; the earlier BCR-ABL fusion discoveries (Rowley, Groffen, Baltimore) are outside the supplied names and may be viewed as precedent.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of follow-up confirm durable survival benefit; the field is fully mature. Prior prizes in adjacent areas may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Relation to earlier cytogenetic and oncogene prizes could count against it.
Sawyers' role is in resistance and next-generation drugs, less central than Druker and Lydon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one. It is a clean mechanistic-to-clinical story with clear patient benefit, and also relevant for neurology.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the evident pair. Others at Ionis, Biogen and the original SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) lie outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical data and independent follow-on therapies; maturity is good, though still relatively recent.
uncertainties: SMN1 gene discovery and gene-therapy approaches are separate contributions that may be contested.
Long-term durability data are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defined a central nutrient-sensing growth-control pathway with implications for cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. The discovery is fundamental and original, with real but heterogeneous clinical use (rapalogs).
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and is the clear primary contributor; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin target binding is also decisive. Sabatini's mTORC1 work is important but I would not add him given scientific-conduct concerns I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed in many systems over thirty years; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Role of Brown, Sabatini and Heitman in the target identification is debated.
Therapeutic success of rapalogs outside transplantation is modest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PCSK9 links human genetics, from gain-of-function hypercholesterolaemia to loss-of-function protection, to approved LDL-lowering drugs. It is a good example of human-genetics target validation with clinical benefit in cardiovascular disease.
assessment.attribution: Abifadel and Boileau first reported the gain-of-function mutations; Seidah identified PCSK9 biochemically; Hobbs and Cohen provided loss-of-function and population evidence. Credit among five is difficult, and the trio I pick leaves out the original disease-gene discovery, which is a serious weakness.
assessment.maturity: Antibody and siRNA drugs are approved, and outcome trials confirm benefit; mature.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Abifadel and Boileau may be unfair.
Statins already made the earlier prize area crowded, so novelty relative to existing recognition is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: APP mutations in familial Alzheimer's disease founded the amyloid-cascade model and motivated disease-modifying antibodies. The genetic discovery is original and high impact, although the overall amyloid hypothesis remains debated.
assessment.attribution: Goate (first pathogenic APP mutation) and Hardy (APP genetics and the amyloid hypothesis) are the pair given; other contributors such as Glenner, Masters and Selkoe are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Anti-amyloid antibodies show modest clinical benefit; confirmation of the causal model is strong in genetics but incomplete clinically, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy of amyloid removal is modest.
Whether the amyloid cascade is a complete explanation is disputed.
